title: Text Diffusion — Brendan O’Donoghue, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A DeepMind research scientist explains text diffusion as an alternative to autoregressive generation: start from noise, iteratively denoise a whole token block, enabling bidirectional self-correction, adaptive compute, and in-place editing, at the cost of lower batch throughput. It is a model-architecture research talk with no deployable tooling for agent orchestration.

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue low-latency models suit unbatched, on-device/interactive use, while high-throughput autoregressive models suit batched server serving; pick per deployment context rather than one model everywhere.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what's that trade-off is on-device applications... you're not batching with thousands of other queries
takeaways.numbers: Gemini diffusion demo hit ~2,000 tokens/sec; 24 passes for 256 tokens vs 256 sequential passes

takeaways.technique: Adaptive compute budget per task difficulty
takeaways.what_they_do: Train/instruct the model to decide its own stopping point so easy prompts use few denoising steps and hard ones use more, roughly monotonic quality gains with more steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for easy responses, it can use a little bit of compute and for harder responses, it can take longer
takeaways.numbers: 100 digits of pi: 4 steps; FizzBuzz: 18 passes; quantum explainer: 31 steps

takeaways.what_they_do: Bidirectional refinement lets the model revise an early answer after completing downstream reasoning, fixing mistakes an autoregressive model commits to.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it had a mistake twice, 60 and then 49, but once it finished the reasoning, it was able to return back and fix the mistake
takeaways.numbers: GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash both failed the same arithmetic prompt the diffusion model self-corrected

takeaways.technique: In-place targeted editing instead of full regeneration
takeaways.what_they_do: Diffusion edits only the wrong span while conditioning on surrounding context, rather than regenerating the whole output token by token.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's not just one by one generating all the tokens. It's doing a clever editing procedure to to actually fill in the uh the correct edits
